reader_question: Where did each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committee send what it raised?
grade_line: Documented: the committees’ reports to the Federal Election Commission
title: The Harris Victory Fund sent $899.4 million to 53 committees in the 2024 cycle, and the Trump National Committee JFC sent $273.8 million to two.
measure_line: Dollars each 2024 presidential nominee’s joint fundraising committee transferred to other committees (line 22 of its reports), 2023 to 2024 election cycle, not adjusted for inflation; a link’s width is its dollars, on one scale for both
notes: Each nominee had more than one joint fundraising committee. Each drawn here is the one that sent its nominee’s campaign the most, read the same way for both; the nominees’ other such committees sent the Harris campaign $4.9 million and the Trump campaign $160.9 million.
A joint fundraising committee raises money for several committees at once and splits it among them by agreement, so a transfer passes on money raised for the committee that gets it.

The 51 state party committees include the District of Columbia’s, and the download lists each with its transfers. Drawn here are transfers, line 22 of each committee’s reports, where a joint fundraising committee reports the shares it passes on. On the same reports, the Harris Victory Fund also paid three of the committees drawn $27.1 million for operating expenses (line 21B), $12.0 million of it to the campaign and $15.1 million to the Democratic National Committee, and refunded $81,000 to two committees that had given to it (line 28C), which the table sets apart. The Trump National Committee JFC’s payments to its two committees were all transfers.
alt: Two committees side by side, each a bar with links to bars for the committees it transferred money to, every bar as tall and every link as wide as its dollars on one scale. The Harris Victory Fund sent $528.7 million to the Harris campaign, $189.3 million to the Democratic National Committee and $181.4 million to 51 state party committees, $899.4 million in all. The Trump National Committee JFC sent $246.8 million to the Trump campaign and $26.9 million to the Republican National Committee.
chart_notes: The chart draws both committees alike, in one ink, on one scale: each bar is as tall as the dollars it sent or received, and each link as wide as the dollars it carried.

notes_internal: Maker B, round 3. Data plan row 94 with change 8, rule 14.104. Data lead ruling (a): no named mark, both committees as a set; (b): both drawn alike, side by side from 680 px (one under the other below, each source's words heading its block under 420 px); every node edge and link in the party-mark ink (money spent to elect a candidate, Rule 14.6's list), node words in the text's ink; one linear unit for both, $4 million a pixel, with a key of three widths; Harris's 51 state party committees fold into one node and the table lists each.
